title: The same forever (Hebrews 13:1–8)
hook: keep loving; show hospitality; remember prisoners; Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today and forever
tomorrow: what do you write first to friends scattered far from home?

segments.voice: A week in Hebrews. A priest who always lives to pray. Laws written on their hearts. Stir up love, so keep meeting. The evidence of things not seen. Others, of whom the world was not worthy. And yesterday's shout: lift the hands that hang down. Now the letter's last chapter, and it reads like a note stuck to the fridge.
screen: `HE ALWAYS LIVES TO PRAY` · `ON THEIR HEARTS` · `STIR UP LOVE` · `NOT SEEN` · `NOT WORTHY` · `LIFT THE HANDS` → `A NOTE ON THE FRIDGE.`

segments.voice: The doorbell. A delivery driver in the rain, a new kid at the lunch table, the neighbor you've waved at for a year and never met. Who might be an angel at your door, and how would you know? Hebrews answers, and the answer is: you wouldn't. "Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares." Unawares. Nobody got a sign. They just opened the door.

The whole list is like that: people easy to forget. It opens, "Let brotherly love continue." Then strangers. Then prisoners: "Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body." Not pity from a distance. As if the chains were on your own wrists, because you have a body too. Then money: "be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee." Contentment rests on a promise, not a balance. And then one sentence standing on its own: "Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever." Look how this week ends where it began. It opened with a priest who never hands off, and it closes on the same one, unchanged. Guests come and go. Prisoners wait. Teachers pass on. Hebrews sets one who doesn't change in the middle of all of it, and hangs the whole list on him.
screen: `LET BROTHERLY LOVE CONTINUE.` · `AS BOUND WITH THEM.` · `I WILL NEVER LEAVE THEE.` · `THE WEEK ENDS WHERE IT BEGAN.` · then, large: `THE SAME FOREVER.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring to mind someone who is locked up tonight, someone you know or someone you'll never meet. Rest your wrists on your knees and keep that person company, as bound with them, until the bell.
The same forever. Hebrews thirteen: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and today, and forever, set in a list about guests and prisoners.
Hold on to this: the same forever, closing Hebrews the way the week opened. Rest well.

howItsDone: Christians visit and pray for prisoners through church prison ministries, welcome guests and newcomers, and some churches carve Hebrews 13:8 over a door or an altar.

fork.setup: a new family moves in across the street, and their kid stands alone at the bus stop every morning. you don't know them at all. what fits Hebrews 13?
options: wait until you're sure they're safe and worth it.
say hello; some have entertained angels unawares.
leave it to the church; welcome is a pastor's job.
fork.reveal: be not forgetful to entertain strangers: Hebrews asks for the welcome first, without a sign or a guarantee.

original.note: Greek: the same. Hebrews 13:8, Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today and forever.

trapdoor: what you thought: the same forever means nothing ever changes.
what it means: in a world of guests, prisoners and teachers who come and go, Hebrews sets one who doesn't change at the center.
what a scholar hears: Hebrews opens with a priest who abideth continually (7:3) and closes on the same one, the same yesterday, today and forever (13:8).
guess: Jesus, unchanged while everything around him changes
a promise that your life will never change
the rule that church worship must never change
recall: the evidence of things not seen
lift the hands that hang down

chat.says: pop can't do stairs at his house. he's moving in with us. into MY room. i said yes but ugh.
options: Saying yes is the love part. Hebrews 13: let brotherly love continue, and be content with what you have.
Then say no. Hebrews 13 says making room is only for strangers, not for your own family.
The ugh cancels it. Hebrews 13 says a welcome only counts if you never feel any cost.
chat.meaning: Hebrews 13 asks for love that keeps going and contentment with what you have, resting on a promise: I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.

bonds.meaning: chains; here, being held in prison
